business_problem: Mercedes-Benz needed to digitalise global product development, connect development, procurement, production, sales, and after-sales data end to end, and help teams make better decisions earlier so new products and technologies could reach series maturity faster without compromising quality or safety.
solution_summary: Mercedes-Benz’s PLM.AI is an in-house, AI-native product lifecycle management backbone for global vehicle development. It ingests and connects development information with procurement, production, sales, and after-sales data through standardized data models and end-to-end integration, creating an intelligent knowledge base and seamless digital thread. CONTACT Elements provides the open PLM core layer that integrates product data, processes, and applications, giving Mercedes-Benz a modular and scalable foundation for future AI technologies. On top of that foundation, PLM.AI coordinates AI agents and AI-powered simulations that analyze cross-functional trade-offs such as cost, crash behavior, hardware and software effects, and production impacts. Siemens contributes AI-enabled design, simulation, and digital validation capabilities for the digital twin so engineering domains can work from a shared data and process foundation. The resulting insights are served back to development teams for earlier validation, faster coordination, and quicker progression to series maturity.

data_flow: Mercedes-Benz connects development data with procurement, production, sales, and after-sales information through standardized data models in PLM.AI. CONTACT Elements provides the shared PLM core where product data, processes, and applications are integrated. AI agents and AI-powered simulations run on that digital thread, and the resulting cross-domain insights are delivered back to development teams and later linked with product, service, and operating data in after-sales.
business_outcome: Mercedes-Benz says PLM.AI can bring new technologies to series maturity up to 30 percent faster, deliver efficiency gains of up to 50 percent in individual engineering processes, and over time could reduce physical testing by half through earlier analysis and validation.

"This can reduce development time by up to 30 percent, with efficiency gains of up to 50 percent expected in individual engineering processes."
